channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Female artisanal miners report sexual violence in Kono district
item.description: Women working in the diamond-rich Jaiama Nimikor area describe systemic rape and harassment while scavenging for gold and diamonds in abandoned pits.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning causes deforestation
item.description: Environmental agency confirms burning of economic trees threatens food security and exacerbates climate change effects.

item.title: African youth protest governance amid economic hardship
item.description: Protests erupted in Kenya, Tanzania, Morocco and other nations as citizens questioned growth figures.

item.title: Mauritius cabinet weighs lowering criminal responsibility age
item.description: Government considers prosecuting 12-year-olds after riots, but legal experts cite lack of evidence and system strain.

item.title: Air Mauritius reports Rs 4.1 billion profit for 2025-2026
item.description: The national airline's positive equity of Rs 1.37 billion returns after being negative since the Covid-19 pandemic.

item.title: Brahimi scores twice to lead Al-Gharafa to victory
item.description: Algerian international Yacine Brahimi scored two goals in the final 10 minutes of the match.

item.title: Sowore, police give conflicting accounts of Ekiti restaurant incident
item.description: Presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore claims a violent attack, while police report a minor altercation and injury.

item.title: Police sergeant accused of shooting woman remains in custody
item.description: Sergeant Gautam Singh Taukoor faces charges of intimidation and involuntary wounding after an incident on October 9.

item.title: Saudi Arabia bans travel from Kenya over Ebola fears
item.description: The kingdom suspended citizen travel and halted all visa issuances due to nine confirmed cases.

item.title: Niger journalist Moussa Kaka detained for two months
item.description: Reporters Without Borders reports that Moussa Kaka has been held incommunicado since August 31.

item.title: Semia Setti's new novel sells out at Tunis book fair
item.description: The author's second book, "Je suis née à six ans," explores childhood trauma and self-reconstruction.

item.title: Tunisia signs stadium reconstruction contract
item.description: A Chinese consortium will rebuild the El Menzah Olympic Stadium for up to 600 million dinars.

item.title: Madagascar university officials detained over fake diplomas
item.description: Three leaders at Itasy University in Soavinandriana face pre-trial detention for alleged diploma fraud.

item.title: Sonatrach raises LPG prices for November
item.description: Algeria's national oil company increased propane by $155 to $825 per ton and butane by $300 to $1050 per ton.

item.title: DR Congo families urged to rebuild state values
item.description: Academics and NGO leaders call for families to instill civic and moral values for national reconstruction.

item.title: Man denies paternity of child heard through rumours
item.description: A 23-year-old man told the Kabushi Local Court he cannot accept responsibility for a child he only heard about from neighbours.

item.title: UN mission mandate expires in Western Sahara
item.description: The UN Security Council failed to renew the mandate for the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara.

item.title: Benin bishops announce African traditional religion conference
item.description: The conference, scheduled for November 19-20, 2026, aims to foster mutual understanding between faiths.

item.title: Malawi Law Society questions president's power to postpone Parliament
item.description: The society argues President Mutharika lacks constitutional authority to direct the Speaker on parliamentary sittings.

item.title: IEBC defends CEO shortlist over foreign applicants
item.description: The electoral commission states all shortlisted candidates for Chief Executive Officer are Kenyan citizens.

item.title: Uganda Tourism Board secures AFCON 2027 marketing deal
item.description: The board will use the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations to promote Uganda's tourism attractions internationally.

item.title: Bandits kill 62 in Taraba market attack
item.description: Armed bandits on motorbikes stormed Binnari community, opening fire on residents and traders.

item.title: N'Djaména mayors meet on local taxes
item.description: A new framework aims to improve coordination and resource sharing among the capital's 10 districts.

item.title: Namibia allocates N$179m for FMD fight
item.description: Lawmakers question if the funding is sufficient to support farmers facing disease and drought.

item.title: Namibia remembers sanitation pioneer Libertina Amathila
item.description: Former deputy prime minister Amathila, Namibia's first woman doctor, drove to eliminate bucket toilets.

item.title: DR Congo prime minister submits 2027 budget to assembly
item.description: Judith Suminwa Tuluka presented the draft finance law for the upcoming fiscal year on October 31, 2026.

item.title: Salim Saleh found Besigye near death in prison
item.description: Retired General Caleb Akandwanaho revealed he intervened to get medical attention for opposition leader Dr Kizza Besigye.

item.title: Mauritius vegetables fail pesticide tests
item.description: Official reports show 59% of fruits and vegetables sold between October 2025 and June 2026 did not meet safety standards.

item.title: Chad faces rising deaths amid health crisis
item.description: Hospitals overflow and funerals increase as authorities report only 14 deaths.

item.title: Malawi U-15 finish 79th at World Cup
item.description: The team secured 15th place in Tier C after beating Rwanda 2-0 in their final match.

item.title: US donates technology to Madagascar health ministry
item.description: American officials provided digital tools to support frontline health workers in data collection and transmission.

item.title: Chad ministry bans justice movement march
item.description: The Ministry of Public Security prohibited the Mouvement national pour la justice march scheduled for October 31, 2026.

item.title: Senegal commission rejects budget bill again
item.description: Lawmakers cite concerns over energy sector funding and potential fuel shortages.

item.title: ECOWAS court presses Togo on constitutional reform
item.description: The regional court sent a reminder to Togo's Justice Minister about its January 29, 2026 ruling.

item.title: Sky Energy launches 100 electric taxis in Malawi
item.description: The company also unveiled 40 charging stations and a ride-hailing app to combat fuel shortages.

item.title: Cape Verde's education system needs reform
item.description: The current system, rooted in the slave era, is insufficient for economic autonomy and national transformation.

item.title: Eswatini seeks E3.79 billion in new loans
item.description: Government plans to borrow up to E1.6 billion from Standard Bank for infrastructure and social projects.

item.title: High Court allows widow to lead church
item.description: Sibongile Dlamini will temporarily remain leader of Faith Christian Fellowship Church after a court ruling.

item.title: Eswatini forum to rethink urban finance
item.description: Municipalities will explore bonds and public-private partnerships to fund development beyond property rates.

item.title: Dominic Kunene to coach Sihlangu again
item.description: The Eswatini Football Association appointed Kunene as interim head coach for a friendly against Malta.

item.title: Man sentenced for four murders
item.description: Vusi Mncina received multiple sentences for murder and attempted murder in Ezulwini.

item.title: UN extends Libya mission to October 2027
item.description: Security Council resolution backs efforts to unify state institutions and hold elections within two years.

item.title: Macron, Nawrocki skip Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics
item.description: Senegal's President Diomaye Faye will host the games without two key foreign leaders due to domestic crises.

item.title: MTN Ghana mobile money transactions grow 44.4%
item.description: The company plans to invest US$1.1 billion over three years to expand network infrastructure and digital services.

item.title: Prime Minister demands swift Vigário Balanta death probe
item.description: Ilídio Vieira Té expresses concern over the slow progress in the investigation into the activist's March death.

item.title: China reaffirms ties and multilateralism with Lesotho
item.description: Ambassador Yang Xiaokun urged local media to respect China's sovereignty claims over Taiwan.

item.title: Senegal ONAS nears completion of 98% of flood control work
item.description: The National Sanitation Office has spent 250 million FCFA on four micro-projects ahead of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games.

item.title: Burkina Faso opens international craft fair
item.description: The Salon international de l'artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO) will run from October 30 to November 8, 2026.

item.title: Guinea's Syli Junior wins UFOA-A U20 title
item.description: Aboubacar Keïta scored the only goal in the 40th minute to secure a 1-0 victory over Gambia.

item.title: Burkina Faso trains 40 specialists on strabismus care
item.description: The Burkinabe Society of Ophthalmology is conducting a training session in Ouagadougou to improve the management of eye misalignment.

item.title: Guinea minister suspends Siguiri governor and 21 officials
item.description: Minister Djenabou Touré suspended the interim governor, four prefects, and 17 sub-prefects on October 30, 2026.

item.title: Four arrested for leasing land to illegal miners
item.description: Unit committee members allegedly took money from galamsey operators who degraded land near Abesua bridge.

item.title: Morocco envoy calls Algeria's Sahara-Palestine comparison shameful
item.description: Omar Hilale accused Algiers of exploiting humanitarian arguments and restricting refugee rights in Tindouf camps.

item.title: Rémy Ayayos Ikounga named deputy grand master of Congo's Masonic lodge
item.description: Colonel major Rémy Ayayos Ikounga replaces Jean-Dominique Okemba, who was removed in April.

item.title: Burundi U15 team loses to Canada in FIFA tournament
item.description: The Burundi U15 team was eliminated from the FIFA U15 World Cup Festival after a 7-0 loss to Canada in Division D quarter-finals.

item.title: Mauritania ministries sign deal to aid farmers
item.description: The environment and agriculture ministries agreed to protect farmlands in Oualata under the 'Mbedra' project.

item.title: Maïmouna Diakhaby appointed head of Port of Conakry
item.description: President Mamadi Doumbouya names strategy advisor to lead the autonomous port authority.

item.title: Angolan NGOs demand electoral probe
item.description: Three civil society groups asked prosecutors to investigate alleged failures in the voter registration process.

item.title: Senegal court seeks one year jail for student death
item.description: A military court in Dakar heard the case of Fallou Sène, who died in 2018 clashes at Gaston Berger University.

item.title: Algerian-born entrepreneur aims to replace keyboard with AI
item.description: Neil Zeghidour, backed by Nvidia, is developing voice AI to make human-machine interactions more natural.

item.title: RPF youth meet in Poland to discuss development
item.description: RPF Secretary General Christophe Bazivamo urged young members in Europe to take practical action for Rwanda's development.

item.title: Cadbury Nigeria profit hits N10.1 billion
item.description: The company's nine-month earnings surpass its entire 2025 profit, with gross margins improving.

item.title: Nigeria begins N50,000 monthly cash payments to vulnerable citizens
item.description: The Federal Government launched a new relief programme to cushion the effects of rising living costs.

item.title: Chinese firm considers CFA88 billion sugar and rice investment
item.description: Nanning Agricultural Development Group seeks feasibility study for plantations and a processing complex in Cameroon's East Region.

item.title: Russia vetoes UN resolution on Western Sahara
item.description: Moscow blocks US proposal to change MINURSO mandate, citing imbalance in negotiations.

item.title: Kaloum FC held to draw by SOAR Académie
item.description: The team drew 0-0 for the sixth consecutive match, remaining third in Ligue 2.

item.title: Sudan offers Russia Red Sea investment, mining
item.description: Sudan's military leader proposed a free economic zone and opportunities in gold, copper, and other minerals to Russian investors.

item.title: European Union gives Mauritania 20 million euros for surveillance
item.description: The funds will provide non-military equipment to boost the army's territorial monitoring capabilities.

item.title: Burkina Faso reinstates death penalty
item.description: The People's Legislative Assembly voted unanimously to bring back capital punishment for terrorism and treason.

item.title: Tunisia and Russia discuss cooperation after Africa summit
item.description: Foreign Minister Nafti met Russian Ambassador Zolotov to follow up on the Russia-Africa summit and strengthen bilateral ties.

item.title: Mauritania plans new diaspora policy
item.description: Foreign Minister Ould Merzoug announced direct consultations with Mauritanians abroad to shape national policy.

item.title: Two Sierra Leone police officers to study forensic science in India
item.description: The officers will gain advanced knowledge in scientific evidence analysis and modern crime detection techniques.

item.title: Managem's weight in MASI index falls
item.description: The mining company's weighting in Morocco's stock market index dropped from 10.5% to 6.9% after annual adjustments.

item.title: Comorian youth learn Chinese history
item.description: Delegations attended lectures on the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference and visited the Communist Party Museum.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea president urges Africa to transform raw materials locally
item.description: Obiang Nguema Mbasogo stated at the Russia-Africa summit that Africa must move beyond exporting raw materials and develop its own industries.

item.title: Algerian physicist's life becomes book at SILA 2026
item.description: Author Rym Khelil will present "Nour. Noureddine Melikechi" at the Algiers International Book Fair.

item.title: Security guard jailed for stealing CCTV camera
item.description: Alie Sesay received a six-month sentence for taking a camera valued at Le2,540 in Freetown.

item.title: Ex-minister threatens retired general over coup allegations
item.description: Musa Ecweru warned Lt Gen Peter Elwelu to surrender within 24 hours or face death if cornered.

item.title: Morocco coach Ouahbi names squad on November 4
item.description: Mohamed Ouahbi will announce the list of players for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Niger.

item.title: Companhia Industrial da Matola challenges import rules
item.description: The Cereals Institute seized 3,300 tonnes of wheat and blocked imports after the company filed a court challenge.

item.title: FBI shares data on Ivory Coast financial court corruption
item.description: Ivorian gendarmes arrested one person after receiving information from the FBI about a corruption network within the financial court.

item.title: Ghana vows justice for teen shot in New York
item.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa contacted the victim's father to offer government support.

item.title: Hilton opens first hotel in Guinea
item.description: The 196-room DoubleTree by Hilton Conakry Kaloum is set to open in 2029.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea to launch cocoa processing factory in six months
item.description: The government aims to transform raw cocoa into paste for chocolate production, boosting national resources.

item.title: Tanzania marks one year since deadly election violence
item.description: Thousands killed in protests suppressed by security forces, with victims still traumatised and critics facing charges.

item.title: Coris Bank launches Islamic finance window in N'Djamena
item.description: The new Coris Bank International Baraka Tchad agency offers deposit, financing, and leasing services based on Islamic principles.

item.title: Japan gives Senegal four ambulances for youth Olympics
item.description: The vehicles will boost health services during the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games.

item.title: Moroccan professor reinvents teaching with AI
item.description: Safaa Makati, a professor at ISGA, is adapting her methods to integrate generative artificial intelligence into her classroom.

item.title: Zinder hosts military training competition closing ceremony
item.description: 12 delegations from defense and security training schools competed in the first edition of the Minister of State for National Defense Cup.

item.title: Sports betting models show varying predictions
item.description: Two models can offer different win probabilities for the same match, with differences explained by calculation methods and data used.

item.title: GETESA sponsors AI Business Malabo 2026 event
item.description: The event on October 28 and 30 explored artificial intelligence opportunities for businesses.

item.title: Niger leaders pray for peace
item.description: Maradi mosque held collective prayers for national stability and protection of authorities.

item.title: Namibia loses N$67.8bn to illicit financial flows
item.description: The finance minister warned that unlawful activities like tax evasion and money laundering deprive the nation of funds for public services.

item.title: Lagos Fashion Week returns for 15th edition
item.description: Africa's largest fashion event showcases dozens of Nigerian and African designers with a focus on sustainability.

item.title: Ethiopians flee border gunfire into Kenya
item.description: Over 36,000 people, mostly women and children, have crossed into Kenya seeking refuge from fighting.

item.title: Fugitive Duqow saves 40 Somali soldiers
item.description: Duqow, a man sentenced to death, rescued soldiers lost after fighting Al-Shabaab in Lower Shabelle.

item.title: Manga schools receive garden fencing materials
item.description: 10 schools in Manga received fencing materials to secure their school gardens and support canteen food supplies.

item.title: Benin women's handball team draws Egypt for Africa Cup
item.description: The Amazones will face Egypt, Congo, and Cape Verde in Group A of the 2026 tournament in Tunisia.

item.title: Kosmos Energy donates 10 ambulances to Sao Tome and Principe health ministry
item.description: The vehicles will bolster the national health system's response capacity and improve patient transport.

item.title: Mali street drug sales endanger health
item.description: Health professionals warn of treatment failures and poisonings from unregulated medicines sold without prescriptions.
